belief: Worrying about money shows I'm being responsible.
origins: Worry can feel like a form of caring. If we stop worrying, we fear we will stop paying attention. Parents who fretted about money may have modeled it as the mark of a serious person, and sometimes worry did seem to get things done. Over time, the habit can become automatic and exhausting.
teaches: Jesus asks, “Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?” and tells us, “Do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself.” Paul says, “Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.” Peter says, “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” Responsibility is planning, budgeting, and acting. Worry does none of these.
self_statements: If I stop worrying, I will get careless.
Good providers lose sleep over money.
I have to think about it constantly.
errors: Believing I must either worry or be careless.
Insisting that I should feel anxious to prove I care.
questions: Has worrying ever solved a money problem, or did actions solve it?
What is the difference between worrying and planning?
Who modeled money worry for me?
What does Jesus say worry can add?
What action steps could replace worry about this problem?
What would it look like to pray and plan instead of worry?
truth: Worry is not the same as responsibility. Planning, budgeting, and acting are responsible, and I can do them with prayer and thanksgiving instead of anxiety. God’s peace can guard my heart while I take wise steps.
hw_truths: Worry adds nothing to my life.
Planning is responsible, worry is not.
God’s peace guards my heart and mind.
I can cast my anxiety on Him.
Today has enough trouble of its own.
log: Each time you worry about money, write one action step you can take and one request you will bring to God.
actions: Give yourself 15 minutes a day to think about money, then set it down.
Turn each worry into a specific task with a date.
Present one request to God and name one thing you are thankful for.
prayer: Lord, I confuse worry with responsibility. Teach me to plan wisely and to bring my requests to You with thanksgiving. Let Your peace guard my heart and mind. Amen.
hw_questions: Has worry ever solved a money problem?
What is the difference between worry and planning?
What request can I bring to God?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can pray and plan, and God’s peace will guard my heart.”
